chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Mi'zam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Hamzah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): I postpone the fasting of three days in each month until winter, then I fast them. He said: 'There is no harm in that.'

key_terms.ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ: Three days (referring to the 13th, 14th, and 15th of the lunar month)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can I delay fasting the three white days of the month to another season?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential flexibility (*rukhsah*) regarding the timing of the monthly *Ayyam al-Beed* fasts, allowing believers to defer them to winter to mitigate the physical hardship of summer heat. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that while the specific days are recommended, the spiritual benefit is preserved even when the fast is shifted to a more manageable season, reflecting the principle of ease in worship.
